children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Safety of foreign exchange reserves is the most important consideration before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) because reserves are ultimately borrowed funds that have to be handled very carefully, deputy governor Rohit Jain said on Thursday.

Return should not be the only consideration while deploying these reserves, which is why a lot of care is taken when allocating the funds, he said. Jain, who is responsible for the departments of external investments, foreign exchange and risk management, among others, was responding to a question by the State Bank of India managing director Ravi Ranjan at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave. "We track market variables and parameters very closely.

We keep on the lookout for better opportunities," Jain said. "The principal considerations in managing forex reserves are three-safety, liquidity and return. All three are important but the order is also important. Safety, liquidity and return (in that order). Because these are borrowed funds, these forex reserves have to be handled very carefully."

title: Safety Comes First in Forex Handling: RBI Dy Guv Jain
